payload.name: Expand health-incident queries with diagnostic terms
payload.description: When a question asks what health scares, medical incidents, or health problems a person or group experienced, retrieve memories that name specific conditions or symptoms, not just memories using the phrase 'health scare'.
content: When the question asks about health scares, health incidents, medical problems, or illnesses experienced by one or more named people, do not rely only on generic 'health scare' or 'health issue' vocabulary. Run additional keyword or structured searches using concrete medical condition and symptom terms (diagnoses, body-part pains, ER or hospital events) and predicate values such as 'health_issue'.
For multi-person questions, run separate searches for each named person in addition to the combined query, because a single combined query can fail to surface each person's specific incident.
Before answering, verify that every named person in the question has retrieved evidence; if a person is missing, issue additional varied searches before finalizing the answer.

solves: Questions asking what health scares or medical incidents someone experienced can fail when supporting memories record specific diagnoses or symptoms instead of the generic phrase 'health scare'. The diagnosed agent stopped after one broad search and answered from vague health-state memories, missing concrete incident memories for both people. Future questions of this type will benefit from expanding retrieval to diagnostic/symptom vocabulary and from searching for each named person separately before answering.
